questions.q: What does passing `false` as the `allOrNone` argument to `Database.insert()` do?
options: It cancels the insert entirely and returns an empty list
It allows records that pass validation to be committed while failing records are skipped, with no exception thrown
It forces every record to fail so you can test your error handling
It is identical to omitting the argument
questions.explain: allOrNone = false enables partial success: valid records save, invalid ones are reported in the result array, and no DmlException is thrown.

options: Whether the entire batch succeeded
Whether that specific result element's corresponding record was saved successfully
Whether the org is within its daily API limits
Whether a trigger fired on the record
questions.explain: Each SaveResult element corresponds positionally to one input record, and isSuccess() reports on that one record.

questions.q: Which result class has an `isCreated()` method that the others don't?
options: Database.SaveResult
Database.DeleteResult
Database.UpsertResult
Database.MergeResult
questions.explain: Database.UpsertResult adds isCreated(), which distinguishes a new insert from an update to an existing record — a distinction only upsert needs to report.

options: A list of all fields on the sObject, regardless of the error
The field name(s), if any, that caused the error
The field-level security settings for the current user
The number of fields that were successfully updated
questions.explain: getFields() returns the field name or names identified as the cause of that particular error.

questions.q: If you call `Database.insert(accts)` with no second argument, how does it behave?
options: It throws a compile error because allOrNone is required
It behaves like allOrNone = true by default: any failure throws a DmlException for the whole batch
It behaves like allOrNone = false by default
It silently ignores failing records
questions.explain: When allOrNone is omitted, it defaults to true, so the call behaves like a plain DML statement — any failure throws a DmlException.
